description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities. Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the Grant Obligations and Conditions, the obligatory dates for submission of the annual/additional reports are mentioned. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
**Result 1:** 100% completed.
Education programmes have improved to better address issues related to risk, land and water management for sustainable agricultural production.
Under this result, we focused on the improvement of the technical, and agronomic knowledge regarding bio-horticulture of the teaching staff of 7 institutions as well as the key policymaking body of the Ministry of Agriculture. The modules were very much focused on sustainable land and water management as well as input management.
**Result 2:** 100% completed
Development of training of trainers programmes in sustainable organic agricultural production and business development, based on the competence-based training concept.
Under this result, we invested in the capacity of CFPA Manouba as a professional education institution in terms of ;
- developing a good knowledge of e-learning and blended learning systems and adaptation of content
- upgrading the didactical skills of staff
- investing in better audio-visual facilities, including better connectivity for e-learning and blended learning programs

The image/table depicts the development of the various modules, the period in which they have been developed/thought, and the level of realization. All training activities have been completed as well as the development and hand-over of teaching materials. Staff was also trained in didactical methods and online education. The only thing that remains is the investments, which will be completed by Q3 2022.
Output 1(80%): ‘Education programs have improved to better address issues related to risk, land and water management for sustainable agricultural production’. The project has supported 8 institutions and has contributed to the improvement of an educational program consisting out of 8 modules. In addition, ICT facilities and connectivity via fibre optic cable have been developed to enable online education. These investments are now being reviewed and will be installed by Q3 2022.
Output 2(100%): ‘Development of train-the-trainer programs in sustainable BIO-agricultural production and Business development, based on the concept of competency-based training’. As part of this result the following results have been achieved by the project so far: 34 staff trained in 8 modules covering bio horticulture, didactics, and entrepreneurship.

comment.narrative: Un programme compréhensif mais des parties du programme seront incluses dans les programmes de formation horticole et de durabilité existants de CFPA Manouba

10-03-2023: 1)Gestion de Sol, 2) Gestion des pratiques d’apprentissage en ligne «E-learning», 3) Pépinière et choix des plants, 4) Irrigation, Installation et entretien, 5) Horticulture Sous Serre, 6) Post-récolte, 7) L’agriculture en tant qu’entreprise, 8) Développement des petites affaires.
The modules regarding entrepreneurship and bio-horticulture will be integrated into the curriculum of CFPA Manouba and offered as a specific, optional module at CAP and DTP levels, within the general horticulture education. Graduates will get a certificate. They have also laid the foundation for a separate program regarding bio-horticulture, to be developed in close collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture. The materials that were handed to CFPA Manouba will also be used to develop modules for blended learning.

comment.narrative: 28 enseignants formés sur les 8 modules techniques par Holland Green Tech (résultat 1) + 16 enseignants formés aux aspects pédagogiques et didactiques de l'éducation en ligne (résultat 2)
10-03-2023: This number is cumulative. On average, the training was followed by about 20-25 participants of which > 80% were female.
10-12-2022: At least 34 people have been trained, with a minimum of 15-20 participants per training. The composition of the participants varied per training topic.

comment.narrative: 10-03-2023: This activity included the refurbishment and equipment for an audiovisual teaching facility for e-learning and blended learning, a fibre-optic cable and some laptops.
10-12-2022: CFPA Manouba has received an investment in the optimisation of their ICT and internet connectivity facilities to assure the feasibility of online education
